items.title: Remove the fixed-length truncation so late-diverging rejection reasons keep distinct digests
items.context: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:479 truncates the normalized reason to 200 characters before hashing. ProofStory gap lists share a preamble longer than that, so two different gaps hash identically. Hash the full normalized reason, retaining only a large sanity bound to cap CPU on pathological input.
items.userSees: node packages/main/dist/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.js prints a passing check stating that two real DEV-gate rejection renders differing only past the former 200-character cut produce different digest keys.

happy.desc: gateFailureDigest applied to two reconstructions of the real DEV-gate rejection render (machine.ts:179 preamble plus renderProofStoryDiagnosticReport), identical for their first 244 normalized characters and differing only in the outstanding gap codes, returns two different keys.
The same two rejections routed through bumpGateFailureCount leave maxGateFailureCount at 1, so assessBreaker does not trip, which is the actual operator-visible consequence.

edge.desc: A rejection reason far longer than any realistic gate message still produces a digest, and the retained sanity bound is exercised rather than silently absent.
Two reasons that are identical up to the sanity bound and differ only beyond it are documented as collapsing, so the bound's residual behavior is stated rather than assumed away.

adversarial.desc: Restoring only the fixed-length truncation makes the new smoke assertions fail, proving the check is bound to this change and not to some unrelated property.

verificationEvidence.note: NOT DELIVERED AS ORIGINALLY WRITTEN, recorded as such: the C1 class was fixed on main by B-cc54, whose prefix and signals-fold this branch adopts untouched. items.title: Narrow the path normalizer to machine-specific absolute roots only
items.context: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:475 rewrites any slash-bearing token, collapsing DEV/REVIEW with DEV/TEST and src/core/alpha.ts with src/core/beta.ts. Restrict it to absolute paths anchored at machine-specific roots so relative repo paths and slash-bearing identifiers stay distinct while host-varying paths still collapse.
items.userSees: The convergence-breaker smoke prints passing checks stating that DEV/REVIEW and DEV/TEST digest differently, that two files under a shared first path segment digest differently, and that the same lock path under /Users and under /private/var still digests identically.

happy.desc: Two rejection reasons differing only in a slash-bearing identifier (the phase pair DEV/REVIEW versus DEV/TEST) produce different digest keys.
Two rejection reasons naming different repo-relative files under a shared first segment (src/core/alpha.ts versus src/core/beta.ts) produce different digest keys.

edge.desc: The same logical lock path rendered under a machine-specific root (/Users/... versus /private/var/...) still produces one digest key, so host-varying paths keep collapsing.
A path that begins at a machine-specific root but continues into repo-relative segments is normalized once, without leaving a partially-rewritten remainder that could differ per host.

adversarial.desc: Restoring the greedy slash-anchored regex makes the new distinctness checks fail while the machine-path collapse check keeps passing, proving both directions are independently bound to this change.

verificationEvidence.note: 'must-differ phase-pair [guard: path-rule-overreach]' asserts DEV/REVIEW and DEV/TEST digest differently, printing both compared values literally. Recorded by case name and guard tag as a WHOLE SET, with no hand-written totals: every figure a reader might want comes from a command in this record, not from prose.

'must-differ in-repo-file-path [guard: path-rule-overreach]' asserts two files under a shared first segment digest differently. Recorded by case name and guard tag as a WHOLE SET, with no hand-written totals: every figure a reader might want comes from a command in this record, not from prose.

'must-still-collapse machine-absolute-path' and 'delimiter-attached-absolute-path' [guard: path-rule-collapse] assert host-varying absolute paths still share one key and still trip the brake. Recorded by case name and guard tag as a WHOLE SET, with no hand-written totals: every figure a reader might want comes from a command in this record, not from prose.

'must-still-collapse machine-path-into-repo-relative-segments [guard: path-rule-collapse]' asserts a path continuing from a machine root into repo-relative segments is consumed in one match. Since the id guard became a whole-token test, a machine path can no longer be protected as an id at all, so the two rules no longer interact. Recorded by case name and guard tag as a WHOLE SET, with no hand-written totals: every figure a reader might want comes from a command in this record, not from prose.

Two revert-proofs, one per direction, re-derived from scratch after the balanced-strip change: widening the path rule to main's slash-anywhere form fails the path-rule-overreach cases, and deleting it fails the path-rule-collapse cases. No subset was carried forward from any earlier round. Recorded by case name and guard tag as a WHOLE SET, with no hand-written totals: every figure a reader might want comes from a command in this record, not from prose.

items.title: Narrow the numeric normalizer to standalone numbers only
items.context: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:476 rewrites digit runs inside identifier tokens, collapsing CHK-001 with CHK-002. Restrict it so digits attached to an identifier survive while free-standing counters such as attempt numbers still collapse.
items.userSees: The convergence-breaker smoke prints a passing check stating that a rejection naming CHK-001 and one naming CHK-002 digest differently, alongside a passing check that two attempts differing only in a free-standing counter still digest identically.

happy.desc: Two rejection reasons differing only in an identifier-embedded ordinal (CHK-001 versus CHK-002) produce different digest keys.

edge.desc: Two rejection reasons differing only in free-standing counters and an ISO timestamp still produce one digest key, so genuine retries of one failure keep accumulating.
A story id such as B-bf52, whose digits are attached to an identifier, survives normalization, so rejections naming different stories are not conflated.

adversarial.desc: Restoring the unconditional digit-run rewrite makes the identifier-ordinal distinctness check fail while the free-standing-counter collapse check keeps passing.

verificationEvidence.note: Cases guarded substantive-id-allowlist assert that an ordinal naming WHICH lifecycle artifact failed survives normalization: 'checklist-ordinal', 'checklist-ordinal-at-reason-start', 'finding-ordinal' and 'unfixed-bug-ordinal'. Cases guarded substantive-id-wrapper-pair-strip and substantive-id-sentence-punct-strip prove the whole-token test is not TOO strict, keeping a real id protected when a real rejection wraps it in balanced punctuation or ends a sentence with it. 'must-still-collapse bare-attempt-ordinal [guard: digit-rule-collapse]' asserts two attempts differing only in a free-standing counter still share one key and still trip the brake, matching the frozen userSees; 'lease-heartbeat-age' and 'lane-counts' extend the same direction. The substantive-id guard is now a WHOLE-TOKEN test rather than a boundary assertion, because boundary assertions leaked four times to four different punctuation shapes. Six cases pin it: 'embedded-test-output-hyphen-compounds' and 'embedded-test-output-slash-joined-names' [guard: substantive-id-token-head-exact]; 'embedded-test-output-digit-letter-tail', 'embedded-test-output-slash-welded-tail', 'embedded-test-output-dot-welded-tail', 'embedded-test-output-hyphen-welded-tail' and 'embedded-test-output-non-ascii-welded-tail' [guard: substantive-id-token-tail-exact]; 'embedded-test-output-doubled-prefix' [guard: substantive-id-doubled-prefix]; 'embedded-test-output-repeated-qualifier' [guard: substantive-id-qualifier-bounded]. Two honest costs are pinned rather than hidden: 'verification-intent-ref-lane-suffix' records that a colon-SUFFIXED composite such as an intentRef loses protection and ties with main — closing it would re-admit the colon as an interior welding character and reintroduce the F-051 defect class — and 'requirement-ordinal-past-window' records the req- window cost. Three review-bookkeeping ids stay collapsed under review-bookkeeping-not-allowlisted; the tag's comment was corrected after measurement showed adding rl- alone fails nothing, because machine.ts:646 welds it behind an equals sign. Recorded by case name and guard tag, no hand-written totals, as a WHOLE SET against the current matrix; the command names the suite that actually demonstrates the claim.

Twenty revert-proofs re-derived from scratch on an isolated copy of the built normalizer, none carried forward: dropping the head anchor fails four cases; the tail anchor six; the doubled-prefix lookahead one; the qualifier one; making the qualifier repeatable one; disabling the leading-punctuation strip two; disabling the trailing strip six. The two strips are NOT independent and that is recorded rather than implied. Emptying the allowlist and making the placeholder index decimal both fail the same eleven cases and are indistinguishable by case name — stated as such, because that claim previously had no case behind it. items.title: Extend the convergence-breaker smoke with a substantive-versus-incidental digest matrix
items.context: packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts:180-182 asserts distinct reasons do not accumulate but uses fixtures too short and too plain to reach any collapse rule. Add the four must-differ cases (long-preamble ProofStory gaps, phase pair, checklist ids, in-repo file paths) and the three must-still-collapse cases (timestamps and attempt counters, machine-specific absolute paths, hex digests), each driving the real bumpGateFailureCount and maxGateFailureCount path so the counter consequence is proven, not just the hash.
